title: Claude for Developers
subtitle: From client to working app: specify, design, code, deploy and hand over
audience_line: Anyone who wants to build applications with Claude, coding basics included
overview: This programme takes participants from what an LLM can and cannot do to an application delivered to a client. They learn the coding basics and build their own Claude system: memory, skills, connected tools, guardrails and token habits. With it they follow the whole path: client meeting, specification book, structure and plan, UI/UX, code, tests, deployment, change request and handover. They finish with a project of their own.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Beginner and junior developers, students, freelancers, entrepreneurs and technical staff

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: Comfortable computer use and basic written English. No coding or AI background needed

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 30 h: 27 h of chapters + 3 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: About one third explanation, two thirds practice on a guided client app, then an individual project

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: One laptop per participant with VS Code, Git, Node and Claude Code; a paid Claude plan (Pro minimum); free GitHub and hosting accounts; a starter repository with login and database already wired

facts.label: Official resources
facts.value: Claude Academy free courses and the official Claude Code documentation

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A validated practice in each phase and an individual project presented live; certificate of completion

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants turn a client need into a specified, designed, tested and deployed application, and explain what Claude built

phases.name: First Steps
phases.intro: What an LLM is, what it can and cannot do, and how to work with it.

chapters.title: LLMs: What They Can & Cannot Do
chapters.content: How an LLM is trained and writes token by token. Strengths and limits: invented facts and libraries, knowledge cutoff, limited context, flattery, bias, and what tools add. How to work with one: what to delegate, how to describe it, how to check it, who stays responsible.

chapters.title: Prompting, Context & Tokens
chapters.content: Chat, Cowork or Code: which one for which job. Privacy and confidential code. Prompting: goal, context, example, constraints, definition of done; letting Claude interview you. Tokens, plan limits, /model, effort and economical habits.

labs.goal: By the end of this phase, participants know when to trust Claude, how to brief it and what uses up their plan.

items.title: Find the limits
items.goal: See for yourself when to trust an LLM and when to check.
items.material: Claude; eight test questions from the trainer, code included.
items.steps: 1) Predict where Claude will fail. 2) Test facts, recent libraries, counting and a bug. 3) Name the cause of each failure. 4) Retry with context or a tool. 5) Sort ten development tasks.
items.result: A trust map: delegate, check or keep.

items.title: Clear prompts, fewer tokens
items.goal: Get a better answer for less usage.
items.material: Claude; the usage screen; three weak development prompts.
items.steps: 1) Set privacy. 2) Rewrite the three prompts. 3) Run one task on two models, with full and reduced context. 4) Compare quality and usage.
items.result: A prompt library and a "which model, which effort" card.

labs.validation: A trust map and three improved prompts.

phases.name: Basics & System
phases.focus: Code, Git, memory, tokens, skills, MCP
phases.intro: Enough code to read and judge what Claude writes, then a Claude system that is used in every later phase.

chapters.title: Coding Basics
chapters.content: How an app works: frontend, backend, database, API. Reading code: variables, types, conditions, loops, functions. Files, packages and error messages.

chapters.title: Claude Code & Git
chapters.content: Terminal and editor. Git: commit, branch, undo, GitHub. The agent loop, Plan mode, Auto mode and the other permission modes, /rewind and /resume.

chapters.title: Project Brain & Token Optimisation
chapters.content: /init and a short CLAUDE.md. Rules by path, Auto memory, start-here and handoff files. /context, /usage, /clear, /compact, targeted reads and short outputs. Output styles and Status line.

chapters.title: Skills, MCP & Plugins
chapters.content: How Skills load and how to write one. The many skills available for each job: specification, design, code, testing, security, deployment. MCP, Plugins and the Plugin marketplace. Six checks before installing: need, source, upkeep, permissions, token cost, overlap.

labs.goal: By the end of this phase, participants can explain simple code and have a working Claude system.

items.title: Read it before you delegate it
items.steps: 1) Predict what it prints. 2) Run it. 3) Fix the bug without AI. 4) Change one rule. 5) Explain each block, then ask Claude to question you.
items.result: A fixed program, explained line by line.

items.title: Build, break, recover
items.goal: Stay in control of a coding agent.
items.material: Claude Code, Git, an empty folder.
items.steps: 1) Plan a small feature. 2) Build and commit it. 3) Request a bad change. 4) Use /rewind, then Git, to undo. 5) Close and /resume.
items.result: A versioned feature and an undo card.

items.title: Teach it once
items.steps: 1) Run /init and shorten the result. 2) Add a rule. 3) Set a style and a status line. 4) Measure the context and reduce it. 5) Restart from a handoff note.
items.result: A lean project brain, tested in a fresh session.

items.title: Build your toolbox
items.material: A scorecard and a selection of famous repositories.
items.steps: 1) Write a specification skill and test its trigger. 2) Score four repositories. 3) Install one. 4) Connect one MCP server. 5) Measure and remove what does not pay.
items.result: An own skill and a justified toolbox.

labs.validation: A program explained without AI and a configured, versioned project.

phases.name: Client to Plan
phases.intro: No code before the need is understood, written, agreed and planned.

chapters.title: Client & Offer
chapters.content: Preparing and leading the first meeting. Users, real problem, constraints, priorities and MVP. Estimate, hosting and AI costs, schedule, revisions and offer.

chapters.title: Specification Book
chapters.content: Scope, roles, user stories, business rules, edge cases, security, personal data, languages and performance. Testable acceptance criteria. From the client document to SPEC.md; method kits compared.

chapters.title: Structure
chapters.content: Architecture and stack choice, components, data model, roles, API contract, folders, environments and secrets. Short decision records.

chapters.title: Plan
chapters.content: Milestones, small ordered tasks, a check for each, dependencies, risks and follow-up. Reviewing a plan made by Claude.

labs.goal: By the end of this phase, participants turn a conversation with a client into documents that Claude can build from.

items.title: The first meeting
items.goal: Agree on what will and will not be built.
items.material: A client played by the trainer; Claude as assistant.
items.steps: 1) Prepare the questions. 2) Interview the client. 3) Summarise the need. 4) Cut it down to an MVP. 5) Present an estimated offer.
items.result: A meeting report and an accepted offer.

items.title: Write what will be built
items.goal: Produce a specification that both client and Claude understand.
items.material: The meeting report and the skill from 2.4.
items.steps: 1) Let Claude interview you. 2) Generate the book with the skill. 3) Remove what was invented. 4) Add acceptance criteria. 5) Have the client sign and derive SPEC.md.
items.result: A signed specification book and SPEC.md.

items.title: Shape the app
items.goal: Decide the structure before the code.
items.steps: 1) Compare two architectures. 2) Draw the chosen one. 3) Define tables and endpoints. 4) Adapt the folders and CLAUDE.md. 5) Record three decisions.
items.result: A design file and a repository skeleton.

items.title: From spec to backlog
items.goal: Make the work small enough to verify.
items.steps: 1) Generate the plan. 2) Split large tasks. 3) Give each a pass or fail check. 4) Trace each requirement to a task. 5) Validate with the client.

labs.validation: A specification book, a structure and a backlog approved by the client.

phases.name: Code & UI/UX
phases.intro: The app is designed and built task by task on the starter repository, with a check after each step.

chapters.title: UI/UX & Frontend
chapters.content: User journeys, wireframes, a small design system and design skills. Components, screens, forms, loading, empty and error states, responsive design and accessibility.

chapters.title: Backend & Database
chapters.content: Tables, migrations, endpoints, validation, login and roles, secrets, connection to the screens. Your own MCP server: when it is useful and how little code it needs.

labs.goal: By the end of this phase, the main journey of the client app works from screen to database.

items.title: Design, then build the screens
items.goal: Turn the journey into usable screens.
items.material: The starter repository, the backlog and a design skill.
items.steps: 1) Draw the journey and wireframes. 2) Choose colours, type and components. 3) Build the screens. 4) Test on phone width. 5) Correct after the client review.
items.result: The main screens, approved by the client.

items.title: Make it work end to end
items.material: The starter database and login; an MCP server template.
items.steps: 1) Add the tables. 2) Build the endpoints. 3) Enforce the roles. 4) Connect the screens. 5) Expose one function to Claude through the MCP template.
items.result: A working main journey and a one-tool MCP server.

labs.validation: The main journey demonstrated and explained by the participant.

phases.name: Check & Deliver
phases.intro: "It looks done" becomes "it is proven and online".

chapters.title: Test, Review & Secure
chapters.content: Unit and end-to-end tests, debugging from the root cause, code review against the specification, security review. Hooks, the PreToolUse hook, deny rules, prompt injection and Sandboxing (macOS, Linux, WSL2).

chapters.title: Deploy & Automate
chapters.content: Hosting, environments, secrets, migrations, backup, rollback, monitoring. Claude in GitHub Actions and Non-interactive mode. Short demonstrations: Bare mode, Agent SDK, Agent teams, Dynamic workflows and Channels.

labs.goal: By the end of this phase, participants prove that the app works and put it online safely.

items.title: Prove it, then protect it
items.goal: Find the faults before the client does.
items.material: The app, SPEC.md and one planted bug.
items.steps: 1) Test the acceptance criteria. 2) Reproduce and fix the bug. 3) Review against SPEC.md. 4) Run a security review. 5) Add a hook that blocks access to secrets.
items.result: Green tests, a review and a tested hook.

items.title: Put it online
items.goal: Release with a check and a way back.
items.material: GitHub, a free hosting tier and a pipeline template.
items.steps: 1) Set secrets. 2) Deploy to staging. 3) Run the checks in the pipeline. 4) Approve production. 5) Roll back once. 6) Run one check with claude -p.
items.result: A live app and a tested rollback.

labs.validation: Passing checks and a live URL.

phases.name: Client Change, Handover & Demo
phases.intro: The client changes their mind, then receives an app they can use and maintain.

chapters.title: Client Change Shipped
chapters.content: Impact and estimate of a change. Update the specification and plan first. Build in Worktrees, review with Subagents, test and release.

chapters.title: Handover & Demo
chapters.content: User guide, technical documentation, runbook, transfer of access, client training, acceptance, maintenance offer and invoice.

labs.goal: By the end of this phase, participants ship a change safely and close a client engagement.

items.title: Version 2
items.goal: Change the app without breaking it.
items.material: A change request from the client.
items.steps: 1) Estimate the impact. 2) Update SPEC.md and the backlog. 3) Build in a worktree. 4) Review with a read-only subagent. 5) Test and deploy.

items.title: Deliver to the client
items.material: The live app and the acceptance criteria.
items.steps: 1) Generate and check the documentation. 2) Demonstrate each criterion. 3) List access to transfer. 4) Train the client on one task. 5) Sign the acceptance.
items.result: A handover pack and a signed acceptance.

labs.validation: Version 2 online and accepted by the client.

phases.name: Project
phases.focus: An app of their own, presented live
phases.intro: Each participant repeats the path alone on a small need of their choice.

chapters.title: Brief & Build
chapters.content: A real need, a short specification, a plan and a first version built with the system from the course.

chapters.title: Finish & Present
chapters.content: Checks, deployment, live presentation, questions on the code, the choices and the token use.

labs.goal: By the end of this phase, participants prove they can deliver an app with Claude without guidance.

items.title: My own app
items.goal: Go from need to working version alone.
items.material: The starter repository and the participant’s Claude system.
items.steps: 1) Write the need and three acceptance criteria. 2) Plan. 3) Design the main screen. 4) Build the main journey. 5) Commit.

items.title: Show and defend
items.steps: 1) Test the criteria. 2) Deploy. 3) Present in five minutes. 4) Explain one piece of code and one rejected suggestion. 5) Show the token use.
items.result: An app online and a live defence.

labs.validation: Project online, presented and explained. With the phase practices, this earns the certificate of completion.

project.title: My own application
project.brief: A small application for a need chosen by the participant, taken from specification to deployment.
project.stack: Claude Code, the participant’s system, starter repository, Git, free hosting
project.deliverable: The repository, SPEC.md, the live URL and a five-minute demo

portfolio.intro: The guided app and the project leave a method and a system to reuse with a real client.
